subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: One of the stated objects of the Information Technology Act, 2000 is to facilitate the electronic filing of documents and their retention in Government records. In that connection-

options.A: the public cannot be compelled to use the electronic mode only
options.B: the public must use the electronic mode once it has been notified
options.C: the electronic mode is available only to a Government official or agency
options.D: the electronic mode is available only where a digital signature is used

answer_html:
Answer: (A) the public cannot be compelled to use the electronic mode only.

The objects of the Act are to give legal recognition to electronic transactions by recognising digital signatures, to facilitate the electronic filing of documents and their retention in Government records, the public not being able to insist on the use of the electronic mode only, to make consequential amendments to other Acts, and to set up a licensing, monitoring and certifying authority.
topic_text: Objects of the Information Technology Act

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Under the Information Technology Act, 2000 a digital signature certificate is issued by-

options.A: the Ministry of Information Technology of the Government of India itself
options.B: the adjudicating authority appointed for the area in which the applicant resides
options.C: a Certifying Authority licensed by the Controller of Certifying Authorities
options.D: the Controller of Certifying Authorities, appointed by the Central Government

answer_html:
Answer: (C) a Certifying Authority licensed by the Controller of Certifying Authorities.

The Controller of Certifying Authorities is appointed by the Central Government to recognise, license, regulate, standardise and supervise the certifying authorities. It is the Certifying Authorities, who are licensed by the Controller, who issue the digital signature certificate and perform such other acts as the Controller may specify. The Controller does not himself issue the certificates.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Unless the parties otherwise agree, the dispatch of an electronic record occurs when it enters a resource outside the control of the originator, and its receipt occurs when-

options.A: it enters any computer resource of the addressee, whether or not that resource has been designated
options.B: the addressee acknowledges the receipt of the record to the originator in the manner agreed between them
options.C: it enters the designated computer resource, or, where none is designated, when it is retrieved by the addressee
options.D: it is retrieved by the addressee, whether or not a computer resource has been designated for the purpose

answer_html:
Answer: (C) it enters the designated computer resource, or, where none is designated, when it is retrieved by the addressee.

A record is treated as sent by the originator, his agent, or a system programmed by the originator which operates automatically. Dispatch occurs when the record enters a resource outside the control of the originator. Receipt occurs when it enters the designated computer resource, and where no computer resource has been designated, when it is retrieved by the addressee. Unless otherwise agreed, the place of dispatch and the place of receipt are deemed to be the place of business.
topic_text: Dispatch and receipt of an electronic record

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: A body corporate becomes liable to pay damages under Section 43A where-

options.A: it possesses or deals with any personal data at all and discloses it to a third party, whether or not the disclosure has been permitted by the provider
options.B: it possesses or deals with sensitive personal data, is negligent in maintaining reasonable security to protect it, and thereby causes wrongful loss or wrongful gain
options.C: it possesses or deals with sensitive personal data and suffers a breach of that data, whether or not it has been negligent in maintaining reasonable security
options.D: it possesses or deals with sensitive personal data and has failed to publish a privacy policy, whether or not any loss or gain has been caused to any person

answer_html:
Answer: (B) it possesses or deals with sensitive personal data, is negligent in maintaining reasonable security to protect it, and thereby causes wrongful loss or wrongful gain.

Section 43A applies where a body corporate possesses or deals with any sensitive personal data or information, is negligent in maintaining a reasonable security to protect such data or information, and thereby causes wrongful loss or wrongful gain to any person. Where those conditions are met the body corporate is liable to pay damages to the person or persons so affected. Negligence and consequential loss or gain are both essential; a breach alone is not enough.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Section 72A provides for the punishment of disclosure of information in breach of a lawful contract, and prescribes-

options.A: imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years, or a fine not exceeding five lakh rupees, or both
options.B: imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years, or a fine not exceeding three lakh rupees, or both
options.C: imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, or a fine not exceeding one lakh rupees, or both
options.D: imprisonment for a term not exceeding seven years, or a fine not exceeding ten lakh rupees, or both

answer_html:
Answer: (A) imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years, or a fine not exceeding five lakh rupees, or both.

Section 72A provides for the punishment for disclosure of information in breach of a lawful contract, and prescribes imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years, or a fine not exceeding five lakh rupees, or both. This is to be distinguished from Section 43A, which is not a penal provision at all but casts a civil liability to pay damages on a negligent body corporate.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
case_facts_html:
Sahyadri Analytics Private Limited is a body corporate incorporated and located in India. It runs an online health tracking service and, in the course of that business, collects from its users their passwords, credit and debit card information, fingerprints used for authentication, and information relating to their physical and mental health condition.

The company has not so far drafted or published any privacy policy. It proposes to share the data it holds with a third party analytics firm. Its reasonable security practices are modelled on the International Standard IS/ISO/IEC 27001, but the last audit of those practices was carried out two years ago and no significant upgradation of its process or computer resource has taken place since.
question_html: Refer to the case scenario. The Information Technology (Reasonable Security Practices and Procedures and Sensitive Personal Data or Information) Rules, 2011-

options.A: apply to the company, the Rules applying only to bodies corporate and persons located in India
options.B: do not apply to the company, the Rules applying only to bodies corporate located outside India
options.C: do not apply to the company, the Rules applying only to individuals and not to bodies corporate
options.D: apply to the company only in respect of the passwords it collects and to no other category of data

answer_html:
Answer: (A) apply to the company, the Rules applying only to bodies corporate and persons located in India.

The 2011 Rules were notified by the Department of Information Technology on April 11, 2011 vide notification no. G.S.R. 313(E), and they apply only to bodies corporate and persons located in India. The company being incorporated and located in India, the Rules apply to it. Passwords, credit and debit card information, biometric information used for authentication, and information relating to physical, physiological and mental health condition are all within the categories treated as sensitive personal data or information under Rule 3.

Its reasonable security practices are modelled on the International Standard IS/ISO/IEC 27001, but the last audit of those practices was carried out two years ago and no significant upgradation of its process or computer resource has taken place since.
question_html: Refer to the case scenario. Under Rule 4 the company is under a duty to draft a privacy policy, make it easily accessible to those providing the information, and publish it clearly on its website. That policy must state-

options.A: the type of information being collected and the identity of every third party to whom that information may hereafter be disclosed
options.B: the purpose for which the information is collected and the period after which the information will be destroyed by the company
options.C: the reasonable security practices undertaken by the company and the name of the auditor who last certified those practices
options.D: the type of information being collected, the purpose for which it is collected, and the reasonable security practices undertaken

answer_html:
Answer: (D) the type of information being collected, the purpose for which it is collected, and the reasonable security practices undertaken.

Rule 4 imposes a duty on body corporates seeking sensitive personal data to draft a privacy policy and to make it easily accessible to those providing the information, and it must be clearly published on the website. The policy should contain details of the type of information being collected, the purpose for which it has been collected, and the reasonable security practices undertaken by the body corporate.

question_html: Refer to the case scenario. Which of the following is among the duties cast on the company by Rule 5 when it collects the information?

options.A: To furnish a copy of the information collected to the adjudicating authority appointed for the area concerned
options.B: To designate a Grievance Officer whose name and contact details appear on the website and who addresses grievances expeditiously
options.C: To obtain the prior approval of the Controller of Certifying Authorities before any sensitive personal data is collected at all
options.D: To retain the information collected for a minimum period of three years from the date on which it was first collected

answer_html:
Answer: (B) To designate a Grievance Officer whose name and contact details appear on the website and who addresses grievances expeditiously.

Rule 5 requires the body corporate to obtain the consent of the persons providing the information; not to collect it unless it is for a lawful purpose and is considered necessary; to use it only for the purpose for which it was collected and not to retain it longer than is required; to ensure that the providers are aware that the information is being collected, of its purposes and recipients and of the name and addresses of the agencies retaining and collecting it; to offer an opportunity to review the information and make corrections; to maintain its security; and to designate a Grievance Officer whose name and contact details are on the website and who is responsible for addressing grievances expeditiously.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
case_facts_html:
Sahyadri Analytics Private Limited is a body corporate incorporated and located in India. It runs an online health tracking service and, in the course of that business, collects from its users their passwords, credit and debit card information, fingerprints used for authentication, and information relating to their physical and mental health condition.

The company has not so far drafted or published any privacy policy. It proposes to share the data it holds with a third party analytics firm. Its reasonable security practices are modelled on the International Standard IS/ISO/IEC 27001, but the last audit of those practices was carried out two years ago and no significant upgradation of its process or computer resource has taken place since.
question_html: Refer to the case scenario. As regards the audit of its reasonable security practices and procedures, the company-

options.A: is in default, an audit being required every six months for any body corporate which handles sensitive personal data
options.B: is in default, an audit being required at least once a year as well as on any significant upgradation of process and computer resource
options.C: is not in default, an audit being required only where the body corporate has undertaken a significant upgradation of its process
options.D: is not in default, an audit being required only once in three years where the standard IS/ISO/IEC 27001 has been adopted

answer_html:
Answer: (B) is in default, an audit being required at least once a year as well as on any significant upgradation of process and computer resource.

Rule 8 provides the reasonable security processes and procedures which may be implemented by body corporates, and the International Standard IS/ISO/IEC 27001 is one such standard which can be implemented to maintain data security. The audit of reasonable security practices and procedures shall be carried out by an auditor at least once a year, or as and when the body corporate undertakes a significant upgradation of its process and computer resource. An audit two years ago, with no upgradation since, does not satisfy the annual requirement.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Business intelligence is-

options.A: a statutory framework for the protection of the personal data of customers held by a body corporate in electronic form
options.B: a single software package which stores the whole of the data of an organisation in one central repository
options.C: an audit technique for verifying the accuracy of the financial statements prepared by a business enterprise
options.D: a technology-driven process for analyzing data and delivering actionable information that helps make informed business decisions

answer_html:
Answer: (D) a technology-driven process for analyzing data and delivering actionable information that helps make informed business decisions.

Business intelligence is a technology-driven process for analyzing data and delivering actionable information that helps executives, managers and workers make informed business decisions. As part of the process organizations collect data from internal IT systems and from external sources, prepare it for analysis, run queries and create data visualizations, dashboards and reports, and make the results available to business users for operational decision-making and strategic planning.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: In the business intelligence process, KPI stands for-

options.A: key process instructions
options.B: known performance intervals
options.C: key planning instruments
options.D: key performance indicators

answer_html:
Answer: (D) key performance indicators.

KPI stands for key performance indicators. The distribution of key performance indicators and other findings to business users is the third of the four steps in the business intelligence process, the others being data preparation, analytical querying of the prepared data, and the use of the information to help influence and drive business decisions.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: The four steps in the business intelligence process are-

options.A: data preparation, analytical querying, distribution of key performance indicators and other findings, and use of the information
options.B: data collection, data storage in a warehouse, data visualisation on a dashboard, and archival of the data so visualised
options.C: analytical querying, data preparation, use of the information, and distribution of key performance indicators to users
options.D: data mining, predictive modelling, what-if analysis of business scenarios, and reporting of the results to the management

answer_html:
Answer: (A) data preparation, analytical querying, distribution of key performance indicators and other findings, and use of the information.

The steps are data preparation, in which data sets are organized and modelled for analysis; analytical querying of the prepared data; distribution of key performance indicators and other findings to business users; and use of the information to help influence and drive business decisions. Before the data can be used, raw data from different source systems generally must be integrated, consolidated and cleansed using data integration and data quality management tools.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Business intelligence data is typically stored in-

options.A: a data warehouse built for an entire organization, or in smaller data marts holding subsets of business information
options.B: a data mart built for an entire organization, or in smaller data warehouses holding subsets of that information
options.C: the transactional database of the source system itself, no separate repository being required for the purpose
options.D: a spreadsheet maintained by each business unit, consolidated at the year end by the business intelligence team

answer_html:
Answer: (A) a data warehouse built for an entire organization, or in smaller data marts holding subsets of business information.

Business intelligence data is typically stored in a data warehouse built for an entire organization, or in smaller data marts that hold subsets of business information for individual departments and business units, often with ties to an enterprise data warehouse. The data can include historical information and real-time data gathered from source systems as it is generated, so the tools support both strategic and tactical decision-making.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Open source business intelligence software typically includes-

options.A: a single version, distributed free of charge, technical support being available from the user community alone
options.B: a single version, licensed on subscription, the source code being released to the subscriber on payment of a fee
options.C: two versions, a community edition free of charge and a subscription-based commercial release supported by the vendor
options.D: two versions, a trial edition free of charge for a limited period and a perpetual licence purchased outright by the user

answer_html:
Answer: (C) two versions, a community edition free of charge and a subscription-based commercial release supported by the vendor.

Business intelligence software that is open source typically includes two versions: a community edition that can be used free of charge, and a subscription-based commercial release with technical support provided by the vendor.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Business intelligence tools which put business intelligence and data visualization functionality directly into business applications, so that users can analyze data within the applications they use to do their job, are described as-

options.A: operational intelligence
options.B: location intelligence
options.C: embedded business intelligence
options.D: collaborative business intelligence

answer_html:
Answer: (C) embedded business intelligence.

Embedded business intelligence tools put business intelligence and data visualization functionality directly into business applications. Collaborative business intelligence is more of a process than a specific technology and combines business intelligence applications with collaboration tools. Operational intelligence, also called operational business intelligence, is a form of real-time analytics delivering information to managers and frontline workers. Location intelligence is a specialized form enabling the analysis of location and geospatial data with map-based visualization.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Cyber crimes can basically be divided into three major categories, namely cyber crimes against-

options.A: data, devices and communication networks
options.B: persons, property and Government
options.C: persons, property and intermediaries
options.D: individuals, companies and regulators

answer_html:
Answer: (B) persons, property and Government.

Cyber crime is a broad term used to define criminal activity in which computers or computer networks are a tool, a target, or a place of criminal activity. Such crimes are basically divided into three major categories: cyber crimes against persons, such as harassment occurring in cyberspace, which may be sexual, racial, religious or other; cyber crimes against property; and cyber crimes against Government, such as cyber terrorism.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Accessing someone's computer without the right authorization of the owner, without disturbing, altering, misusing or damaging data or the system, by using a wireless internet connection, is called-

options.A: vandalism
options.B: carding
options.C: trespass
options.D: squatting

answer_html:
Answer: (C) trespass.

Trespass means to access someone's computer without the right authorization of the owner where the intruder does not disturb, alter, misuse or damage the data or the system, by using a wireless internet connection. Squatting arises where two persons claim the same domain name. Vandalism means deliberately destroying or damaging the property of another, and cyber vandalism the destruction or damage of data when a network service is stopped or disrupted. Carding refers to false ATM, debit and credit cards used by criminals for their monetary benefit.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Which of the following is NOT listed as a cyber crime against Government?

options.A: Piracy of software
options.B: Data alteration
options.C: Cyber terrorism
options.D: Cyber warfare

answer_html:
Answer: (B) Data alteration.

The cyber crimes listed against Government are terrorism, warfare, piracy and unauthorized information. Cyber terrorism is described as a major burning issue of domestic as well as global concern, common forms of attack being distributed denial of service attacks, hate websites and hate e-mails and attacks on sensitive computer networks, all of which endanger the sovereignty and integrity of the nation. Warfare refers to politically motivated hacking to damage and to spy.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Which of the following is NOT a cyber crime under the Information Technology Act, 2000?

options.A: Tampering with computer source documents
options.B: Publishing obscene information in electronic form
options.C: Publishing a false digital signature certificate
options.D: Sending threatening messages by email

answer_html:
Answer: (D) Sending threatening messages by email.

Sending threatening messages by email is dealt with under the Indian Penal Code and not under the Information Technology Act. The cyber crimes listed under the Act are tampering with computer source documents, computer related offences involving data alteration, publishing obscene information, unauthorised access to a protected system, breach of confidentiality and privacy, and publishing false digital signature certificates. The Penal Code was itself amended to bring cyber crimes within its purview, and it covers defamatory messages by email, forgery of electronic records, bogus websites and cyber frauds, web-jacking and e-mail abuse.

subject: Corporate and Economic Laws
question_html: Under the Information Technology Act, 2000, tampering with computer source documents and publishing false digital signature certificates are dealt with respectively by-

options.A: Section 66 and Section 72
options.B: Section 67 and Section 70
options.C: Section 70 and Section 65
options.D: Section 65 and Section 73

answer_html:
Answer: (D) Section 65 and Section 73.

The Act deals with tampering with computer source documents in Section 65 and with publishing false digital signature certificates in Section 73. Section 67 covers publishing obscene information, Section 70 unauthorised access to a protected system, and Section 72 breach of confidentiality and privacy.
